And six months ago, you were right on the money that it was in the spirit of C&C. The patches they've pushed since, though, significantly reduce the importance of base building, render walls a complete waste of resources, and eliminated the differences between the Terran and Beta factions in regards to base defenses. The result of all of this is that focus is placed far more on offensive unit production and turns per minute -- that's why I say it's morphed into a Starcraft Clone. If they had left the game well enough alone, with maybe minor balance fixes, rather than totally redesigning the balance from the ground-up, I wouldn't be so upset that I wasted my money on it, but as-is, I bought four copies that never get used anymore.

Hmm... I see Beta build walls all the time. Aggressive walling is AFAIK still a very viable tactic for Beta. Human walls... well, it was always debatable how useful they were, I suppose.

Eliminated the difference in base defenses? You mean the popcap requirement for Human turrets? I can't say I've seen that come into play much in my own play (FWIW I have 100 some hours in the game which is a lot for me) and Humans are still really the only faction with viable defenses: Beta wall defenses are mostly reactionary imvho where Human players tend to build more and more often.

I think one thing you may be detecting that we agree on is the prevalence of Beta T1/2 units in particular (Commandos, Stalkers etc) as these units, especially with upgrades, can be spammed to great effect (Goo in particular have trouble with exploding commandos). I think unit balance to reinforce the requirement for mixed unit armies is definitely needed, for sure.

For me, I'd like to see more unit variety (check the section in my second article where I talk about unit design to see what I mean in more detail - Tiberian Sun had superior unit design imho) and some increased speed with regards to early game economy - the first couple minutes of matches can be painfully slow. I think even providing players with more off-the-bat resources would be very interesting to try and would likely result in more back-and-forth play and more interesting strategies.

Prior to the rebalance changes, walls were a lot sturdier. All walls and structures have both health and armor ratings in the base config; the changelog for the first round of rebalance patches declared that they were removing the armor modifiers from all walls and base defenses. Whereas on release it was possible, even for Humans, to have a wall with a few turrets hold a chokepoint until reserves could be mustered, such a configuration now barely serves as a speedbump, making investment in such an utter waste. The main reason I see Betas build walls is to get access to the land/air turret unit that can be garrisoned in the towers; that's worth building standalone, one-tile wall structures.

And yes, making Human turrets use popcap completely changed the dynamic for that faction. Previously, the limit to human defense building was capped by resource accumulation. Where before you could fill a map with turrets, or have dozens in reserve ready to teleport ot the front lines, a player now has to decide between base defenses and offensive units -- and given that Human units are made of glass, this change effectively eliminated human defensive structure building.

I don't bemoan people who do like the game. I just think a lot of us were the victim of bait-and-switch, whether intentional or not, as the developers caved to the demands of a majority of the multiplayer community -- a community that clearly wanted something closer to Starcraft than Command and Conquer. At the end of the day, I just wish I'd waited a couple of months before buying the game.
